relevance_note: Single-patient case report of Tangier disease with two ABCA1 variants: "two heterozygous variants in the ABCA1 gene".
method_note: Read the paper directly; no table, all values transcribed by hand into a small build script. Spans keep the Markdown's HTML entities (>, <); values decode them (e.g. variant 'c.1834G>Tp(- Glu612*)', as printed with a fused 'Tp' and a stray '- '). Zygosity 'heterozygous' for each variant from 'two heterozygous variants'; phase/compound heterozygosity is not stated, and no parental testing, variant class or classification is given. Age 43 is at referral ('A 43-year-old woman ... was referred'); it is not stated as age at onset, diagnosis or last evaluation (diagnosis and follow-up came later), so all age fields are 'not reported'. Country not stated for the patient (only author affiliations in Portugal). Vital status not stated explicitly. Absent classic findings ('bright orange tonsils, hepatosplenomegaly, and corneal opacity) were missing') recorded as excluded features; per the narrow/broad rule, absence of hepatosplenomegaly does not exclude splenomegaly or hepatomegaly alone, and absence of orange tonsils does not exclude the composite 'orange-colored or enlarged tonsils', so those checklist items are 'not reported'. 'Other laboratory tests were unremarkable' is a general statement and excludes nothing specific. Total cholesterol 99 and triglycerides 105 mg/dl are given without interpretation, so low LDL and hypertriglyceridemia are 'not reported'. Paresthesia is reported but peripheral neuropathy is not diagnosed for the patient (only stated for the disease in general), so neuropathy is 'not reported'. Periorbital xanthomas mapped to checklist 'skin lipid deposits' (observed). 'Normal biventricular size and function' on the initial echocardiogram was later followed by 'mild dilatation of the left ventricle'; recorded biventricular dysfunction as excluded and LV dilatation as observed (change over time, not a contradiction). Supplementary material is not included in the file. No contradictions found.
